title: RoboLiveMem: Is Robot Memory Solved When the World Does Not Wait?
abstract: arXiv:2611.30047v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Robot agents built on frontier vision-language models now solve most robot memory benchmarks. Does this mean they can remember what they need in a home, where people and machines keep moving things? Existing memory benchmarks cannot answer this question, because they pause the simulator while the model thinks: nothing can change during a decision, so whatever the robot remembers is still true when it acts. We introduce RoboLiveMem, a benchmark that runs the same memory tasks twice, once with the world paused while the model thinks and once with the world running. It contains 29 task families in three tiers, from 16 realistic BEHAVIOR-1K scenes of homes, workshops and a restaurant to controlled ManiSkill tasks. Every task mixes real changes with harmless look-alikes and runs without any change, so that no fixed strategy succeeds, and most tasks have a twin that keeps the change in view, which separates forgetting from acting too late. T

translated_title: RoboLiveMem：当世界不再等待时，机器人记忆问题真的解决了吗？
translated_abstract: 基于前沿视觉-语言模型构建的机器人智能体如今已能解决大多数机器人记忆基准测试。但这是否意味着它们能够在人与机器不断移动物品的家庭环境中记住所需的信息？现有的记忆基准测试无法回答这个问题，因为它们在模型思考时会暂停模拟器：在决策期间一切都不会改变，因此机器人记住的任何信息在行动时依然有效。我们提出了RoboLiveMem，这是一个将相同记忆任务运行两次的基准测试——一次在模型思考时暂停世界，一次让世界持续运行。它包含三个层级的29个任务族，从16个真实的BEHAVIOR-1K家庭、工作间和餐厅场景到受控的ManiSkill任务。每个任务都将真实变化与无害的相似情况混合，并在没有任何变化的情况下运行，使得任何固定策略都无法成功；大多数任务都有一个保持变化可见的孪生任务，从而将“遗忘”与“行动太迟”区分开来。
tldr: 本文提出RoboLiveMem基准测试，通过让相同的记忆任务分别在“暂停世界”和“世界持续运行”两种模式下执行，揭示了现有基于视觉-语言模型的机器人记忆在动态变化的真实环境中的真实局限性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces RoboLiveMem, a benchmark that runs identical memory tasks twice—once with the world paused during model thinking and once with the world running—to reveal the true limitations of current VLM-based robot memory in dynamically changing real-world environments.
